rulings.Case Title: GEOFFREY LYNCH VS. WELLS FARGO BANK, N.A. ET AL
rulings.Calendar Matter: MOTION FOR SUMMARY JUDGMENT Or In The Alternative Summary Adjudication
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Friday, September 11, 2026, 2025, Line 4. Defendant Wells Fargo Bank, N.A.'s unopposed Motion for Summary Judgment or, in the Alternative, Summary Adjudication is GRANTED. (The Court's complete tentative ruling has been emailed to the parties). For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 302 Zoom ID 160 409 7690; Passcode 516287.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept302tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing. Counsel for the prevailing party is required to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the substantive portion of the tentative ruling and must email it to contestdept302tr@sftc.org prior to the hearing even if the tentative ruling is not contested. The court no longer provides a court reporter in the Law & Motion Department. Parties may retain their own reporter, who may appear in the courtroom or remotely. A retained reporter must be a California certified court reporter (CSR), for only a CSR's transcript may be used in California courts. If a CSR is being retained, include in your email all of the following: their name, CSR and telephone numbers, and their individual work email address. =(302/JMQ)

rulings.Case Title: MICHELLE FULLER VS. BAMBOO INSURANCE, LLC
rulings.Calendar Matter: Notice Of Motion And Motion To Compel Plaintiff Michelle Fuller To Respond To Written Discovery Requests
rulings.Rulings: Set for Law and Motion/Discovery Calendar on Friday, September 11, 2026, 2025, Line 1. Defendant Sutton National Insurance Company's Motion To Compel Plaintiff Michelle Fuller To Respond To Written Discovery Requests is GRANTED IN SUBSTANTIAL PART. On June 4, 2026, Defendant served by email Form Interrogatories (Set Four), Special Interrogatories (Set Two), Requests for Admissions (Set Two), and Requests for Production of Documents (Set Two) on Plaintiff Michelle Fuller. Plaintiff failed to serve timely responses to any of Defendant's discovery requests. Nor did Plaintiff provide any responses after Defendant reached out to inquire about status. On this record, the court finds Defendant did not agree to continue the deadline for Plaintiff's responses such that Plaintiff reserved a right to object. Defendant's Requests for Admissions (Set Two) are deemed admitted. (See Code Civil Procedure section 2033.280(b).) Plaintiff has waived all objections and must provide objection-free responses to Defendant's Form Interrogatories (Set Four), Special Interrogatories (Set Two) Requests for Production of Documents (Set Two). (See Code Civil Procedure sections 2030.290(a)&(b), 2031.300(a)&(b), 2033.280(a).) Plaintiff's objection-free responses are due 15 days after notice of entry of this order. Plaintiff's contention that the motion is moot because she will serve compliant responses before the hearing is unavailing. First, even if she had served responses and they were substantially compliant with the Code requirements, the court could still grant the motion. (See Sinaiko Healthcare Consulting, Inc. v. Pac. Healthcare Consultants, 148 Cal.App.4th 390, 407-408 (2007).) In any event, Plaintiff has not demonstrated that she has provided any responses, let alone that they were substantially compliant with the Code. The record does not demonstrate Plaintiff acted with substantial justification. Plaintiff shall pay $1,460 to Defendant Sutton National Insurance Company as sanctions, payable no later than 30 days after notice of this order. (See Code of Civil Procedure sections 2023.010, 2023.030, 2031.300(c), 2031.310(h).) To the extent Defendant requests different or additional relief, the motion is denied. Defendant is ordered to prepare a proposed order which repeats verbatim the above text and email it to contestdept302tr@sftc.org prior to the time set for hearing. For the 9:00 a.m. calendar, all attorneys and parties may appear in Department 302 remotely or in person. Remote hearings will be conducted by videoconference using Zoom. (Dept. 302 Zoom ID 160 409 7690; Passcode 516287.) To appear remotely at the hearing, go to the court's website at sfsuperiorcourt.org under "Online Services," navigate to "Tentative Rulings," and click on the appropriate link, or dial the corresponding phone number. Any party who contests a tentative ruling must send an email to contestdept302tr@sftc.org with a copy to all other parties by 4pm stating, without argument, the portion(s) of the tentative ruling that the party contests. The subject line of the email shall include the line number, case name and case number. The text of the email shall include the name and contact information, including email address, of the attorney or party who will appear at the hearing.
